title: Computer Game Design (Game Design and Implementation)
term: Winter 2015 era (per wiki; course has been taught by other instructors in other years)
instructor: Jeremy Gibson (as of Winter 2015; taught by other instructors, e.g. Austin Yarger, in other years)
workloadNotes: High-workload capstone/MDE elective. Weekly textbook readings and tutorial implementations, recreation of a classic NES-era game in Unity, two rapid prototypes within 2 weeks, weekly project presentations, burndown-chart tracking, short postmortem papers, and a multi-month team project (teams of 4) demoed at an end-of-semester public exhibition, including trailers and peer playtesting/feedback. No formal exams or quizzes reported. Exact grading percentages not documented in this source.
prerequisitesText: EECS 281 (Data Structures and Algorithms) with a C or better, or graduate standing.
textbooks: Jeremy Gibson, Introduction to Game Design, Prototyping, and Development
